# 什么是 CITED 框架？

- 原标题：What Is CITED Framework?
- 作者：Flavio Amiel Roborank 创始人
- 原文更新日期：2026-07-15
- 原文：https://roborank.io/glossary/cited-framework/
- 栏目：[AI Search & GEO](https://roborank.io/ai-search/)
- 说明：中文全文翻译，后附英文原文。原文中的数据、观点、平台说明及推广内容均按原文保留，未经独立验证。

---

## 中文全文

CITED 框架是 Roborank 用于在 AI 搜索中赢得引用的模型，把生成式引擎优化划分为五项影响因素：可信度（Credibility）、可索引性（Indexability）、主题权威性（Topical authority）、实体优化（Entity optimization）和传播分布（Distribution）。每一项都对应一个前提条件，AI 系统在检索页面、并将其作为来源引用进答案之前，会隐式或显式地检查这些条件。

### 核心要点

- CITED 是五项影响因素的首字母缩写：**C**redibility，可信度；**I**ndexability，可索引性；**T**opical authority，主题权威性；**E**ntity optimization，实体优化；**D**istribution，传播分布。
- 五项对应 AI 答案的两个阶段：可索引性和主题权威性决定页面是否被*检索*；可信度、实体优化和传播分布决定检索出的段落是否被*选中并注明来源*。
- 一个页面可以四项很强，却因第五项而不可见。一个可信、切题但屏蔽 AI 爬虫的页面，根本不会进入候选集合。
- CITED 是诊断清单，不是任何 AI 引擎公布的分数。它定位页面*为什么*被引用或未被引用，而非给出排名数字。

### CITED 框架如何运作

AI 答案分两步组装。首先，引擎检索一组候选文档；随后，它从其中少量文档提取段落，综合为回复，并为各段注明来源。页面可能在任何一步失败，而且失败悄无声息：没有什么会告诉你，最佳段落根本没进入候选池，或者虽然被检索却遭到跳过。[生成式引擎优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/)的实践，就是赢下这两步；CITED 框架则把实践拆成五个可以逐一检查的部分。

五个字母大致按引擎遇到这些条件的方式组织。**可索引性**与**主题权威性**决定页面是否会被检索。**可信度**、**实体优化**和**传播分布**决定检索出的段落是否成为模型引用的那一段，以及模型是否足够信任你，愿意把你的名字附在这项说法上。由于这些条件前后相接，它们更像一条链，而不是评分卡：如果第五项断了，其他四项满分也没有意义。框架的作用就是让这个断点显现。

CITED 用于诊断，不是引擎报告的指标。没有 AI 系统会公开一个“CITED 分数”。它提供的是共同语言，来讨论每个内容团队最终都会问的问题：*为什么机器引用他们，而不是我们？* 同时，它让答案指向具体、可修复的缺口，而非模糊感觉。

### 五项影响因素

- **可信度（Credibility）**：说法可信且表达清楚吗？这是最直接掌握在你手中的一项，包括具体数字及其具名出处、直接引语、直白的陈述。它对应[引用就绪度](https://roborank.io/glossary/citation-readiness/)和[可提取性](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/)，让一段文字可以被完整移用，而不会把歧义一并带走。
- **可索引性（Indexability）**：机器能真正到达并读取页面吗？robots.txt 必须允许 [AI 爬虫](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/)，内容渲染不能被一道 JavaScript 墙挡住，页面也必须可索引。这是大门；门关着，其他四项根本没机会被评估。
- **主题权威性（Topical authority）**：网站对主题的覆盖是否足够深入，使检索系统把它视作该查询的相关候选？单薄、孤立的页面很少进入竞争性问题的候选集，而围绕主题形成连贯的内容体系则可以。
- **实体优化（Entity optimization）**：引擎是否把你识别为真实、身份已解析的事物，而非孤立的词串？[实体优化](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-optimization/)把品牌、作者和产品关联到已建立的实体，让模型可以把说法归于一个已经理解的“谁”。
- **传播分布（Distribution）**：你的声誉是否在自己域名之外得到呼应？互联网上的提及、参考和相互印证的来源，会提高模型交叉核查时反复找到你的概率，从而增加你在答案中的[声量份额](https://roborank.io/glossary/share-of-voice/)。

### CITED 框架示例

下面是一个说明性演示，用来观察五项因素如何作用于同一页面。它依据的每个机制都真实存在，并有文档记录。

先看**可索引性**，因为这是大门。页面若想被 ChatGPT 的浏览工具引用，就必须能被 OpenAI 的 user-agent 访问；OpenAI 的文档将 `GPTBot` 与 `OAI-SearchBot` 列为应在 robots.txt 中允许的爬虫，以便抓取这些内容。这里一条禁止指令，就能让后续的一切归零。Google 自己的[爬虫概览](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/overview-google-crawlers)也针对 `Google-Extended` 和 AI 功能记录了同样原则：没有访问，就没有候选资格。

接着看**可信度**。2023 年论文 *[《GEO：生成式引擎优化》](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)* 在保持基础事实不变的情况下，测量哪些内容修改能使生成式引擎更愿意采用某个段落。加入**注明出处的统计数据**、**权威人士的直接引语**和**有权威来源依据的表述**，带来了最大提升：最好的方法让 AI 答案中的可见度最高提高约 40%，论文中的一项可见度指标报告了 **41% 的提升**；关键词堆砌则无效。因此，可信的答案块不只是文风上的讲究，而是拥有最多实测证据支持的单项内容改动。

剩下三项，解释了为什么仅靠可信度无法填补全部差距。**主题权威性**说明，为什么陌生域名上一张优秀的孤立页面，仍难以战胜拥有深厚、连贯主题内容的网站：检索偏爱已建立地位的候选。**实体优化**说明，为什么被识别的品牌会被点名，而无法解析的词串不会：模型可以把说法归于已经理解的实体。**传播分布**则说明站外印证为什么重要：模型交叉核查事实时，会反复落到其他来源也指向的那个来源。把页面逐项过完五个条件，诊断结果很少是“什么都要改”，通常是某个具体字母，而那个字母就是你的上限。

### 人们容易搞错的地方

我见过团队把 CITED 当作内容清单，只做到自己喜欢的字母就停下。他们把大量精力投入可信度：统计数据、引语、清楚的答案块，却从未检查可索引性，结果最希望访问自己的 AI 爬虫，被悄悄挡在 robots.txt 外，再好的文字也没人看见。另一种情况是，可索引性和主题权威性都做好了，却不明白为什么内容深度只有自己一半的对手总被点名。原因是，对手已经是知识图谱中的实体，而自己仍是一串模型无法解析为具体事物的文字。这个框架是一条链，不是菜单。五项中最弱的那个决定上限，而它几乎从来不是你本来就擅长的那一项。

### 常见问题

#### CITED 代表什么？

可信度、可索引性、主题权威性、实体优化和传播分布。它是 Roborank 的框架，用于说明 AI 系统检索页面、并在生成答案中将其引用为来源之前，页面需要满足的五个条件。

#### CITED 框架是 Google 排名因素吗？

不是。CITED 是诊断模型，不是任何搜索或 AI 引擎运行、公布的算法。它把有文档依据的抓取、检索、实体解析和引用行为整理成清单，帮助你逐项找出页面被引用或不被引用的原因。

#### CITED 哪个字母最重要？

对你的页面来说，最弱的那个最重要。它们组成一条链：可索引性决定内容能否被看见，可信度与实体优化决定是否被信任和识别，传播分布强化前两者。最低项限制结果，因此应该先修复它。

#### CITED 与 GEO 有什么区别？

生成式引擎优化是在 AI 答案中获得引用的广泛实践。CITED 是执行它的一种结构化方式，通过五项影响因素，把目标拆成具名、可审计的部分，让团队知道具体应补哪个缺口，而不是泛泛地优化。

### 结论

CITED 把“出现在 AI 答案里”这个模糊目标，拆成五个可以实际审计的问题：机器能到达页面吗，主题覆盖够深入吗，说法是否可信清晰、值得引用，引擎是否认识你这个真实实体，以及这种声誉是否在互联网上得到呼应。沿着这条链工作，先修补最弱的一环。你最不擅长的那个字母，决定了你究竟能不能被点名。

## 英文原文

The CITED Framework is Roborank’s model for earning citations in AI search, organizing generative engine optimization into five levers: Credibility, Indexability, Topical authority, Entity optimization, and Distribution. Each names a prerequisite an AI system checks — implicitly or explicitly — before it retrieves a page and quotes it as a source inside an answer.

### Key Takeaways

- CITED is an acronym for five levers: **C**redibility, **I**ndexability, **T**opical authority, **E**ntity optimization, and **D**istribution.
- The five map to the two stages of an AI answer: Indexability and Topical authority govern whether a page is *retrieved*; Credibility, Entity optimization, and Distribution govern whether a retrieved passage is *selected and attributed*.
- A page can be strong on four letters and invisible on the fifth — a credible, on-topic page that blocks the AI crawler never enters the candidate set at all.
- CITED is a diagnostic checklist, not a score any AI engine publishes; it locates *why* a page is or isn’t cited, not a ranking number.

### How the CITED Framework Works

An AI answer is assembled in two moves. First the engine retrieves a set of candidate documents; then it synthesizes a reply that lifts passages from a few of them and attributes each to a source. A page can fail at either move, and it fails silently — nothing tells you that your best paragraph was never in the candidate pool, or that it was retrieved and passed over. [Generative engine optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/generative-engine-optimization/) is the practice of winning both moves; the CITED Framework is a way to break that practice into five parts you can check one at a time.

The five letters are ordered roughly the way an engine encounters them. **Indexability** and **Topical authority** decide whether a page is retrieved at all. **Credibility**, **Entity optimization**, and **Distribution** decide whether a retrieved passage is the one the model quotes and whether it trusts you enough to put your name on the claim. Because the letters are sequential, they behave like a chain rather than a scorecard: a perfect score on four of them counts for nothing if the fifth is broken. The framework’s job is to make that broken link visible.

CITED is diagnostic, not a metric an engine reports. No AI system exposes a “CITED score.” What it gives you is a shared vocabulary for the question every content team eventually asks — *why did the machine cite them and not us?* — and a way to answer it that points at a specific, fixable gap instead of a vibe.

### The Five Levers

- **Credibility** — Is the claim trustworthy and cleanly stated? This is the letter most under your direct control: specific numbers attributed to a named origin, direct quotes, plain declarative phrasing. It maps to [citation readiness](https://roborank.io/glossary/citation-readiness/) and [extractability](https://roborank.io/glossary/extractability/) — a passage that can be lifted whole without inheriting your ambiguity.
- **Indexability** — Can the machine actually reach and read the page? An [AI crawler](https://roborank.io/glossary/ai-crawler/) has to be allowed in robots.txt, the page has to render its content without a JavaScript wall, and it has to be indexable. This is the gate: if it’s shut, the other four letters never get evaluated.
- **Topical authority** — Does the site cover the subject with enough depth that a retrieval system treats it as a relevant candidate for the query? Thin, one-off pages rarely enter the candidate set for competitive questions; a coherent body of work on the topic does.
- **Entity optimization** — Does the engine recognize you as a real, resolved thing rather than an unattached string of words? [Entity optimization](https://roborank.io/glossary/entity-optimization/) ties your brand, authors, and products to established entities so the model can attribute a claim to a “who” it already understands.
- **Distribution** — Is your reputation echoed off your own domain? Mentions, references, and corroborating sources across the web raise the odds that a model, cross-checking, keeps landing on you — feeding [share of voice](https://roborank.io/glossary/share-of-voice/) in the answers themselves.

### Example of the CITED Framework

The walkthrough below is illustrative — a way to see the five levers acting on one page — but every mechanism it leans on is real and documented.

Start with **Indexability**, because it is the gate. To be quoted by ChatGPT’s browsing tool, a page has to be reachable by OpenAI’s user agents; OpenAI documents `GPTBot` and `OAI-SearchBot` as the crawlers that must be allowed in robots.txt for that content to be fetched. A single disallow line here zeroes out everything downstream. Google’s own [crawler overview](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/overview-google-crawlers) documents the same principle for `Google-Extended` and AI features: no access, no candidacy.

Now **Credibility**. The 2023 paper *[“GEO: Generative Engine Optimization”](https://arxiv.org/abs/2311.09735)* measured which content changes made a generative engine more likely to feature a passage, holding the underlying facts constant. Adding **cited statistics**, **direct quotations from authorities**, and **authoritative sourced language** produced the largest lifts — the best methods raised visibility inside AI answers by up to roughly 40% (the paper reports **+41%** on one visibility metric), while keyword stuffing did not help. So a credible answer block is not a stylistic nicety; it is the single content change with the most measured evidence behind it.

The remaining three letters explain the gap that Credibility alone can’t close. **Topical authority** is why a lone strong page on an unfamiliar domain still struggles against a site with a deep, coherent body of work on the subject — retrieval favors the established candidate. **Entity optimization** is why a recognized brand gets named where an unresolved string does not: the model can attribute the claim to an entity it already understands. And **Distribution** is why corroboration off your own site matters — a model cross-checking a fact keeps landing on the source that other sources also point to. Run a page through all five and the diagnosis is rarely “improve everything.” It is one specific letter, and that letter is your ceiling.

### The thing people get wrong

The mistake I watch teams make is treating CITED as a content checklist and stopping at the letters they enjoy. They pour effort into Credibility — the statistics, the quotes, the clean answer blocks — and never check Indexability, so the AI crawler they most want to reach them is quietly blocked in robots.txt and none of the good writing is ever seen. Or they nail Indexability and Topical authority and wonder why a rival with half the depth keeps getting named: the rival is an established Entity in the knowledge graph and they are a string of text the model can’t resolve to a thing. The framework is a chain, not a menu. The weakest of the five letters is the one setting your ceiling, and it is almost never the letter you were already good at.

### Frequently Asked Questions

#### What does CITED stand for?

Credibility, Indexability, Topical authority, Entity optimization, and Distribution. It is Roborank’s framework for the five conditions a page has to satisfy before an AI system will retrieve it and cite it as a source inside a generated answer.

#### Is the CITED Framework a Google ranking factor?

No. CITED is a diagnostic model, not an algorithm any search or AI engine runs or publishes. It organizes documented behaviors — crawling, retrieval, entity resolution, citation — into a checklist you can work through to find why a page is or isn’t cited.

#### Which letter of CITED matters most?

The weakest one for your page. The letters form a chain: Indexability gates whether content is ever seen, Credibility and Entity optimization gate whether it is trusted and resolved, and Distribution reinforces both. Your lowest letter caps the result, so fix that first.

#### How is CITED different from GEO?

Generative engine optimization is the broad practice of being cited in AI answers. CITED is one structured way to execute it — a five-lever breakdown that turns the goal into named, auditable parts, so a team knows which specific gap to close rather than optimizing in general.

### The Bottom Line

CITED breaks the vague goal of "show up in AI answers" into five things you can actually audit: can the machine reach your page, does it cover the topic deeply, is the claim credible and clean enough to quote, does the engine recognize you as a real entity, and is that reputation echoed across the web. Work the chain and fix the weakest link first — the letter you are worst at is the one deciding whether you get named at all.
